column3: NASB renders “implore” as “request” and “by” as “with regard to.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord”); it renders “in mind” as “from your composure,” “word” as “message,” and “has been present” as “has come.”
NASB follows the critical text (“lawlessness”); it adds “it will not come.”
NASB follows the critical text without “as God”; it renders “named” as “so-called” and “setting forth” as “displaying.”
NASB adds “will do so” and renders “until he may be out of the midst” as “until he is taken out of the way.”
NASB has “the Lord” without “Jesus,” following manuscripts that lack it; it follows the critical text (“slay”) and renders “annul” as “bring to an end.”
NASB adds “that is” and renders “wonders of falsehood” as “false wonders.”
NASB follows the critical text; “in return for which” is rendered “because.”
NASB reads “will send,” the future of other manuscripts; the critical text has the present “sends.” “A powerful delusion” is rendered “a deluding influence.”
NASB follows the critical text; “unrighteousness” is rendered “wickedness.”
NASB reads “from the beginning”; manuscripts differ between this and “as firstfruits.” “Faith of the truth” is rendered “faith in the truth.”
NASB adds “it was” and renders “to the obtaining of” as “that you may gain.”
NASB renders “hold fast to” as “hold to” and adds “of mouth.”
NASB follows the critical text without “you”; “encourage” is rendered “comfort.”
